walkthroughs.body_html:
Your genome is all the DNA in a cell.

DNA is a polymer of two strands forming a double helix, stored in chromosomes in the nucleus. A gene is a section of DNA that codes for a protein.

Genes come in versions called alleles. A dominant allele is expressed if present; a recessive allele only shows when both copies are recessive.

The genotype is the alleles you carry (Bb). The phenotype is what you see (brown eyes).

Variation comes from genes, environment, or both. Mutations create new alleles.

Natural selection: individuals with advantageous alleles survive and reproduce. Over generations this drives evolution.
